findings.title: Federated recovery codes not marked as used after validation
findings.body: In `isValid()` for `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE`, the implementation returns true as soon as the input matches any raw key in `myUser.recoveryCodes.getCredentialData()` but never mutates the stored credential to remove or flag the consumed code. Recovery codes are one-time-use credentials; the local `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider` marks codes as used when validated. Here the same code can be reused indefinitely, so the security guarantee of recovery codes is lost whenever the user lives in federated storage.

findings.title: Federated recovery-codes credential can never be removed
findings.body: Because `isValid()` does not track per-code consumption, the `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` built by `getCredentials()` from the stored raw `credentialData` will always have `allCodesUsed() == false`. Consequently the branch in `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.isRecoveryAuthnCodeInputValid` that calls `credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(...)` will never run for a federated user, so the recovery-codes credential sticks around forever, the user is never re-prompted via `CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES`, and the user storage is never asked to delete the credential.

findings.title: Raw recovery codes persisted in federated credentialData
findings.body: `updateCredential` saves the JSON produced by `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential` (which serializes the raw codes) straight into `credentialData` without hashing. The local `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider` hashes the codes before storage (it relies on `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.hashRawCode` with `NOM_ALGORITHM_TO_HASH`). Storing raw codes in `credentialData` diverges from that posture, so any path that exposes `credentialData` (DB dumps, debug logging, serialized credential model) leaks the user's recovery codes in plaintext. The model reconstructed by `getCredentials()` will also carry these raw codes through `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues`, so callers that read `RecoveryCode.getValue()` get the cleartext code.

findings.title: Test does not verify single-use semantics or credential cleanup
findings.body: `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` only exercises a single successful entry of one recovery code. Given that `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.isRecoveryAuthnCodeInputValid` now also targets federated credentials (via `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential`), the test should additionally assert that (a) re-entering the same recovery code is rejected by the federated validator, and (b) once the last code is consumed, the federated credential is removed and the user is asked to configure new codes. Without these assertions the two real bugs above are not caught by CI.
